finding: The herdr tool's agent_stop gained with_kin=True, but no test fails if it is dropped.
why: All 3 new tests set the herdr detection to 'broken', so they only reach multiplexer._stop_without_tool.
fix: Add one fake-herdr stop test with an orphaned descendant, asserting it is dead after mux('agent-stop', ...).
evidence: herdr.py:311 `none="pane close" if handle else "nothing to kill", with_kin=True)`

finding: A failed or partial kin sweep is silent, so agent-stop can still answer stopped true while an orphan runs.
why: The helper's OSError, timeout or non-zero exit returns [], a failed AttachConsole is skipped inside the helper, and kin() returns [] when the root's creation time cannot be read or drops a member whose creation time cannot be read, so every sweep failure looks the same as 'no kin' and stop() reports 'killed the process tree'.
fix: Make the sweep report 'unchecked' (return None or raise) and have kill_tree/stop add a caveat or a stopped-false reason when the sweep did not run or a console could not be attached.
evidence: except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError): return []  /  return [int(x) for x in done.stdout.split() if x.isdigit()] if done.returncode == 0 else []  /  if mine is None: return []  /  born = None if member in skip else _born(member)

finding: Nothing tests the safety clause that spares the caller and its ancestors.
why: In every new test the pytest caller and its ancestors are older than the root, so deleting `line(os.getpid())` or `line(pid)` fails no test.
fix: Add a test where a process newer than the root shares the root's console or session and is the caller or its ancestor, asserting it is not returned by process.kin.

criterion: Boundary values, empty/null/missing inputs, error and rollback paths, off-by-one, concurrency/ordering, partial-failure handling
finding: kin kills any newer process in a shared console or session whose parent is alive, not only ones whose parent ended; the caller's own siblings and children are not spared
why: The filter is born >= root and not in members, the caller's ancestors or root's ancestors, so a process the caller started after the root, or a sibling of the caller, that shares the root's console or session dies when the root shares the caller's console or session; CONTRACT.md says 'whose parent ended' but no code tests that.
fix: Keep a candidate only when its parent is gone and skip the caller's descendants, or narrow the CONTRACT.md and docstring wording to match what is killed.
evidence: process.py:257-260 `for member in set(_containers(members)): ... if born is not None and born >= mine: out.append(member)`

finding: Possible blurred failure: a console or session member whose creation time cannot be read is dropped from kin without a trace.
why: born is None removes the member from the kill list and from the survivor list, so stop() reports stopped true while that process keeps running.
fix: Return unjudgeable members separately and report them.
evidence: born = None if member in skip else _born(member)

finding: Possible over-kill on POSIX: _born is whole-second ISO text, so a neighbour in the same session born earlier within the root's second passes 'born no earlier than the root'.
why: The age guard has 1 s resolution on POSIX while Windows compares 100 ns ticks.
fix: Compare finer-grained start ticks on POSIX (stat field 22) for the kin filter, or document the 1 s window.
evidence: if born is not None and born >= mine:

finding: Two of the new tests do not wait for the orphan to leave the process tree, so they can pass without the fix.
why: If agent_stop lists the tree before the orphan's parent exits, the orphan is killed as a tree member.
fix: Add `assert wait_for(lambda: orphan not in process.tree(root.pid))` before agent_stop in both tests.
evidence: lines 777-778 and 799-800 go straight to agent_stop

finding: Module docstring says kin is 'a newer process in the root's console', but the code reads the console or session of every tree member.
why: The stale sentence points a maintainer back at the broken design.
fix: Say 'in a console (Windows) or session (POSIX) that a tree member uses'.
evidence: a newer process in the root's console (Windows) or session (POSIX).

finding: Unnamed constants: 0x00000008 (DETACHED_PROCESS) and the 4096 process-list cap in the helper.
why: The silent 4096 cap truncates a larger console list without notice.
fix: Name the flag and either name the cap or retry when GetConsoleProcessList returns more than the buffer.

finding: Possible mysterious names: _born aliases creation_time or _created; _containers returns processes, not containers.
why: A reader must read both bodies to learn which one kin may use.
fix: Name by meaning and give _containers a docstring on POSIX.

finding: The own-pane variant's 'older neighbour survives' assertion cannot fail.
why: The neighbour is started without a new session or console, so it is not in the root's pane console or session; the sweep never lists it. Only the callers-console variant exercises the born-no-earlier filter.
fix: Assert the neighbour assertion only in the callers-console case, or put the neighbour in the root's own console or session so the born-no-earlier filter is exercised.
evidence: assert wait_for(lambda: not process.alive(orphan)) and process.alive(neighbour.pid)

finding: The first new test's cleanup raises ValueError on an empty pid file and then leaks its 300 s processes.
why: `int(grand.read_text())` runs when the file exists but is still empty.
fix: Use the same `grand.exists() and grand.read_text().strip()` guard as the later tests.

criterion: Boundary values, empty/null/missing inputs, error and rollback paths, off-by-one, concurrency/ordering, partial-failure handling
finding: agent-stop can still answer stopped true while an orphan survives, when the orphan's console holds no tree member (inferred, not live-tested)
why: Windows kin finds orphans only through a console some listed member still uses; a command that started a background server and then exited leaves that server alone in a console no member uses, which is the literal A-1 case.
fix: Add a case of a finished command's orphan under per-command consoles; either find such orphans or state the limit in CONTRACT.md and herdr.md.
evidence: process.py:257 `for member in set(_containers(members))` is the only source of kin; adversary A-1: 'A shell call that starts a background server and then exits makes this tree.'
